canonical_name: TÜBİTAK 2204-A Lise Öğrencileri Araştırma Projeleri Yarışması (High School Students Research Projects Competition)
organizer: TÜBİTAK — Bilim İnsanı Destek Programları Başkanlığı (BİDEB)
age_range: no explicit minimum; must not have turned 20 as of the final application day (verbatim: 'yarışma başvuru tarihinin son günü itibarıyla 20 yaşından gün almamış olmalıdır')
grades: high school (lise), both örgün (formal) and açık öğretim (open/distance) systems
international_eligibility: NOT_INTERNATIONAL_BY_DESIGN — eligibility is by WHERE the student is enrolled (Türkiye or KKTC), not citizenship. A foreign national enrolled in a Turkish high school qualifies; a Turkish citizen studying abroad does not.
turkey_access_reasoning: This is Türkiye's own national government-run competition — not an international competition Turkish students must find a route into. Direct eligibility for any student enrolled in a Turkish or KKTC high school.
citizenship_residency_restrictions: Enrollment-based, not citizenship-based. Verbatim (call document §4.1.1): 'Yarışmaya, Türkiye ve KKTC'de örgün ve açık öğretim sisteminde öğrenim gören tüm lise öğrencileri katılabilir.'
qualification_stages: Bölge (regional) exhibition -> national Final. A 4th stage exists for students TÜBİTAK separately selects to send to international competitions (confirmed 2026-08-26 via TÜBİTAK's own EUCYS newsroom post, see unresolved/evidence below) — that stage is NOT automatic from placing at the national final.
fee_note: No fee appears anywhere in the 17-page 2025-2026 call document. TÜBİTAK covers travel/accommodation/meals for students (plus one advisor/teacher) invited to regional and national stages.
financial_aid_if_relevant: N/A — free to enter; TÜBİTAK pays participant travel costs to advance stages.
registration_open_note: 2025-2026 cycle application window has already closed (see cycle evidence below). 2026-2027 cycle not yet announced as of this record's verification date.
deadline_note: No current open deadline. Historical: 2025-2026 cycle ran roughly 13 Oct – 12/19 Dec 2025 (sources differ by exactly a week, likely an extension — see evidence). Next (2026-2027) cycle dates not yet published; TÜBİTAK's own pattern is an October announcement.
competition_dates: Regional and national final dates are set within each annual cycle and published on the competition's own page; not available for a not-yet-announced cycle.
country_location: Türkiye (regional cities + national final location varies by year)
output_award_type: cash prizes + certificates at regional/national level; patent-registration support for national top-three; and — the single highest-value fact in this record — a real Turkish university-admission benefit: (a) §7.1.1 'Ek Katsayı' (extra coefficient on the YKS entrance exam), earned by national top-three placing alone, usable once in the student's first exam year if they choose a related department; (b) §7.1.2 'Sınavsız yerleştirme' (exam-free placement into a related programme via ÖSYM), earned only by placing top-three at an international competition TÜBİTAK separately selected and sent the student to — a materially higher and later bar than the national result. The two benefits must never be collapsed into one sentence.

canonical_name: TÜBİTAK 2202 — Ulusal Bilim Olimpiyatları (National Science Olympiads)
organizer: TÜBİTAK — Bilim İnsanı Destek Programları Başkanlığı (BİDEB), Yarışmalar Grubu
age_range: no explicit numeric age band; gated by grade instead (see grades)
grades: Grades 9-11 for most branches (Mathematics, Geography, Computer Science); grades 5-8 for the two ortaokul/middle-school branches (Middle School Mathematics, Middle School Computer Science). Final-year (12th grade / son sınıf) high school students are EXCLUDED from every branch — decision-critical: a student who waits until 12th grade has permanently missed this route, and with it the route to every TÜBİTAK-fed international science olympiad.
international_eligibility: NOT_INTERNATIONAL_BY_DESIGN — this is Türkiye's own national competition, not an international one requiring a route in.
turkey_access_reasoning: National government competition, enrollment-based (Türkiye or KKTC), open to any eligible-grade student at any school type — this IS the Turkey access point for IMO/IBO/IChO/IPhO/IOI/IOAI, not a competition needing its own route.
citizenship_residency_restrictions: Studying in Türkiye or KKTC (same enrollment-based basis as 2204-A), not citizenship-based.
qualification_stages: Five stages: (1) Birinci Aşama Sınavı — nationwide multiple-choice exam in 81 provincial centres; (2) Yaz Okulu — two-week preparatory summer school; (3) İkinci Aşama Sınavı — written/practical exam, medals awarded (max 4 gold / 8 silver / 12 bronze per branch); (4) Kış Okulu — two-week intensive winter school; (5) Takım Seçme Sınavları — team selection exams determining Türkiye's representatives at regional/international olympiads.
fee_note: Not explicitly stated as free on the official page (unlike 2204-A, which explicitly names TÜBİTAK as covering travel/accommodation/meals). Recorded as NULL rather than assumed free, per the founder's cost-evidence rule — no fee is known to exist for this programme, but silence is not confirmation.
financial_aid_if_relevant: Unknown — not stated on the page retrieved.
registration_open_note: The 34th cycle's first-stage exam was held 2026-05-16 (application deadline updated to 2026-04-21). The 35th cycle's dates were not published as of this record's verification date (2026-08-26) — confirmed still unpublished via fresh fetch today.
competition_dates: Cycle-dependent; not available for a not-yet-announced cycle.
mode: in-person (provincial exam centres; residential summer/winter schools)
country_location: Türkiye (81 provinces for stage 1; specific host locations for the schools/later stages vary by year)
output_award_type: Medals (gold/silver/bronze) at stage 2; ultimately, team selection to represent Türkiye at the international science olympiads (IMO, IBO, IChO, IPhO, IOI, IOAI — each independently confirmed by the respective international body to route through this exact TÜBİTAK site, see the companion upgrade records in this same batch).

evidence.claim: Nine branches, grade eligibility, exclusion of final-year students
evidence.quote: Fresh WebFetch 2026-08-26 confirms the branch list and structure exactly as cr1 recorded 3 days earlier: 'For high school students (grades 9-11): Mathematics, Geography, Computer Science, Physics, Chemistry, Astronomy-Astrophysics, Biology. For middle school students (grades 5-8): Middle School Mathematics, Middle School Computer Science.' Also: '30 yıldır iki aşamalı sınav sistemi ile' — 30-year, two-stage exam structure, with Astronomy-Astrophysics (2022) and Geography (2024) as the newest additions.

evidence.claim: This is the confirmed national route for 5 of 6 TÜBİTAK-linked international olympiads, independently by each international body's own page
evidence.quote: IBO: 'Türkiye: National Biology Olympiad — Established since 1993 — Official website' -> bilimolimpiyatlari.tubitak.gov.tr/tr (ibo-info.org). IMO: sole national link on Türkiye's IMO country page is the same URL (imo-official.org/countries/TUR/). IChO: contacts CSV names TÜBİTAK as institution of Türkiye's first long-term contact (ichosc.org, CSV export). IOI: names the specific Bilgisayar-branch URL, live-checked HTTP 200 (stats.ioinformatics.org/countries/TUR). IOAI: names 'TÜBITAK (The Scientific and Technological Research Council of Türkiye)' as 'Accredited organization' in plain text, Türkiye a founding country (ioai-official.org). IPhO: also names a tubitak.gov.tr link, though that specific URL is dead / 2019-dated — route still usable via the live bilimolimpiyatlari.tubitak.gov.tr site the other five independently confirm.
evidence.url: see companion records S6A-0003 through S6A-0008 in this same file for the full per-body citations, carried forward from cr1_turkey_routes.jsonl CR1-072/073/076/077/078/080, spot-checked, not re-fetched word-for-word today since these are the international bodies' own country-directory pages, not TÜBİTAK's — lower drift risk than a competition's own cycle-status page.
